'''Robert Schleip''' (born 1954) is a German psychologist, [[Human biology|human biologist]] and author, best known for his work in the field of [[fascia]]. He serves as the director of the Fascia Research Group, a research collaboration between the [[University of Ulm]] and the [[Technical University of Munich]]. Schleip is also the founding director of the Fascia Research Society, the research director of the European [[Rolfing]] Association and vice president of the Ida P. Rolf Research Foundation. He is involved in the [[alternative medicine]] field of [[rolfing]].

== Education ==
In 1978, Schleip became Germany's first certified [[rolfer]] at the Rolf Institute and in 1983 became a Certified Advanced Rolfer in the field of [[Structural Integration]].<ref name="auto2">{{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.318.5854.1235 | doi=10.1126/science.318.5854.1235 | title=From Rolfer to Researcher | date=2007 | last1=Grimm | first1=David | journal=Science | volume=318 | issue=5854 | page=1235 | pmid=18033860 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Schleip graduated with a degree in [[psychology]] from [[Heidelberg University]] in 1980.<ref name="auto">{{cite web | url=https://www.daserste.de/information/wissen-kultur/w-wie-wissen/sendung/2012/faszien-104.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170824133852/https://www.daserste.de/information/wissen-kultur/w-wie-wissen/sendung/2012/faszien-104.html | archive-date=2017-08-24 | title=Faszien: Geheimnisvolle Bänder - W wie Wissen - ARD &#124; das Erste }}</ref> From 1984 to 1987 he trained as a [[Feldenkrais]] teacher and became a Certified Feldenkrais Practitioner in the field of Sensorimotor Facilitation from the International Feldenkrais Guild in 1987.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.futurelifenow-online.com/robert-schleip-feldenkrais-summit/ | title=Robert Schleip Feldenkrais Summit • Future Life Now Online }}</ref>{{failed verification|date=June 2025}}

In 2006, he earned his doctorate in [[human biology]] from the [[University of Ulm]].<ref name="auto2"/> That year he received the "Vladimir Janda Prize for Musculoskeletal Medicine" for research he performed with Werner Klingler.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JandaPreis Saeule |url=http://www.somatics.de/JandaPreis_Saeule.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140423004100/http://www.somatics.de/JandaPreis_Saeule.pdf |archive-date=2014-04-23 |website=www.somatics.de}}</ref>

In 2023, he was appointed to a research professorship in the department for Health & Psychology for the university by the Diploma University of Applied Sciences.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.science.de/user/536 | title=Robert Schleip, Dr. Biol. Hum., Dipl. Psych. }}</ref>

== Rolfing ==

Schleip has been a [[rolfing]] instructor since 1988 and maintains a part-time private practice in [[Munich]].<ref name="auto"/> He served as a member on the board of directors for the European Rolfing Association in Munich from 1995 to 1999, and on the ethics committee from 1999 to 2003, as well as a member of the international advisory board of the Rolf Institute in [[Boulder, CO|Boulder]] from 2000 to 2005.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rolfing.org/about-us/our-team | title=Our Team &#124; European Rolfing Association e.V. }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rolf.org/bod.php | title=Board of Directors - Dr. Ida Rolf Institute }}</ref>

In 2006, he became the research director of the European Rolfing Association. He also is vice president of [[Ida Rolf|Ida P. Rolf Research Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rolfing.org/node/3536 | title=Clone of Scientific Research &#124; European Rolfing Association e.V. }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://ntc.ie/team/dr-robert-schleip/#:~:text=Schleip%20is%20an%20Executive%20Research,%2C%20orthopedics%2C%20and%20training%20science | title=Dr. Robert Schleip - NTC - See who you can be! }}</ref> In 2013, he received the RISI Award for "Excellence in Research" by the Rolf Institute.<ref>{{Cite journal| title=The Rolf Institute Membership Conference 2013 | journal=Structural Integration: The Journal of the Rolf Institute | page=48 | volume=41 | number=2 | date=December 2013 | url=https://novo.pedroprado.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Journal_12-13_full.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240712173844/https://novo.pedroprado.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Journal_12-13_full.pdf | archive-date=2024-07-12}}</ref>

== Fascia research==

In 2007, Schleip along with Werner Klingler organized the first Fascia Research Congress, sponsored by the [[National Institute of Health]] and hosted at [[Harvard Medical School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fasciaresearch.de/uni-ulm-internFeb08.pdf|title=Faszien – ein aktives Organsystem|website=www.fasciaresearch.de | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924010546/http://www.fasciaresearch.de/uni-ulm-internFeb08.pdf | archive-date=2015-09-24}}</ref> The conference was covered in a two-page [[Science Magazine]] article titled "Cell Biology Meets Rolfing with a section titled "From Rolfer to Researcher" referring to Schleip's career shift.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.318.5854.1234 | doi=10.1126/science.318.5854.1234 | title=Cell Biology Meets Rolfing | date=2007 | last1=Grimm | first1=David | journal=Science | volume=318 | issue=5854 | pages=1234–1235 | pmid=18033859 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> He has served on the scientific committee for all subsequent congresses (2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2022, 2025) and chaired the 2018 and 2022 congresses.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.fasciaresearchsociety.org/previous_congresses.php | title=Previous Congresses - Fascia Research Society }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kA_UAQAACAAJ | title=Fascia: The Tensional Network of the Human Body : The Science and Clinical Applications in Manual and Movement Therapy | isbn=978-0-7020-7183-6 | last1=Schleip | first1=Robert | last2=Stecco | first2=Carla | last3=Driscoll | first3=Mark | last4=Huijing | first4=Peter A. | date=2022 | publisher=Elsevier }}</ref>

He was a founding member of the Fascia Research Society in 2011 and has served on the board of directors since 2020. In 2023 he received the  designation of founding director.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.fasciaresearchsociety.org/founding_members.php | title=Founding Members - Fascia Research Society }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://fasciaresearchsociety.org/board_and_staff.php | title=Board and Staff - Fascia Research Society }}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{cite web | url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1225-0475 | title=ORCID }}</ref>

Schleip is the director of the Fascia Research Group, a research collaboration between the [[University of Ulm]] (2007-2019) and the [[Technical University of Munich]] (2019–Present).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.fasciaresearch.de/team | title=Team }}</ref>

He is co-founder and co-director of the Institute für Angewandte & Integrative Gesundheitsforschung (IAIG), a research institute directed towards applied and integrative health research under the umbrella of the Diploma University of Applied Sciences in Germany (2024–present).<ref>{{cite web |title=Institut für Angewandte & Integrative Gesundheitsforschung (IAIG) |url=https://www.science.de/forschungsstelle/institut-fuer-angewandte-integrative-gesundheitsforschung-iaig |website=science.de |access-date=26 December 2025}}</ref>

== Fascial Net Plastination Project ==
{{Main|Fascial Net Plastination Project}}
In 2018, Schleip spearheaded the ''Fascial Net Plastination Project (FNPP)'', ananatomical research initiative designed to plastinate and study the human fascial network. The FNPP brought together experts in [[anatomy]], [[dissection]], and [[plastination]], to plastinate a complete human fascia specimen.<ref name="fasciaanatomylabs">{{Cite web |title=About Jihan Adem & Gary Carter - Fascia Focused Anatomy Labs |url=https://www.fasciaanatomylabs.com |website=fasciaanatomylabs.com |access-date=2024-08-26}}</ref><ref name="bowencollege">{{Cite web |title=Jihan Adem |url=https://www.bowencollege.org.uk |website=bowencollege.org.uk |access-date=2024-08-26}}</ref>

The project created a full-body human fascia plastinate named '''FR:EIA''' (Fascia Revealed: Educating Interconnected Anatomy). FR:EIA was unveiled at the 2021 Fascia Research Congress and is currently on display at the [[Body Worlds]] exhibition in Berlin.<ref name="bodyworlds">{{Cite web |title=FR:EIA - Fascial Net Plastination Project |url=https://bodyworlds.com/freia/ |website=Body Worlds |access-date=2024-08-26}}</ref><ref name="abmp">{{Cite web |last=Clauson |first=Rachelle |title=Fascial Net Plastination Project: Revealing the Fascial Network |url=https://www.abmp.com/textonlymags/article.php?article=1922 |website=Associated Bodywork & Massage Professionals |access-date=2024-08-26}}</ref>

== Lecturer ==

From 2005 to 2013, he served as a neurophysiology researcher at the [[University of Ulm]].[23] In 2014, he received a lifelong appointment as Visiting Professor at the Instituto Universitario de Ciencias de la Salud, Buenos Aires.[17]

Since 2019, Schleip has been a Research Associate and, since 2024, a Senior Scientist at the professorship of conservative and rehabilitative orthopaedics in the TUM School of Medicine & Health at the [[Technical University of Munich]].[23]

Since 2019, Schleip has been a professor of conservative and rehabilitative orthopaedics in the Department of Sport and Health Sciences at the [[Technical University of Munich]],<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |title=Robert Schleip |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Robert-Schleip |website=www.researchgate.net}}</ref> and a faculty member at the Diploma University of Applied Sciences.<ref name="auto1"/> In 2023, he was appointed as a professor of health and psychology at the Diploma University of Applied Sciences.<ref name="auto1"/>
